name: Carrion Defense Works Autonomous Wound Treatment System
product_name: Carrion Defense Works Autonomous Wound Treatment System
description: An implantable medical system that automatically detects and treats injuries without conscious intervention. The AWTS consists of a network of subdural sensors that monitor tissue integrity, blood pressure, and chemical markers for injury, connected to micro-reservoirs of hemostatic agents, analgesics, and antibiotics that deploy automatically at wound sites. When the system detects a penetrating wound, it immediately seals the wound channel with hemostatic foam, administers localized pain suppression, and begins antibiotic prophylaxis — all within 2 seconds of injury, before the patient has finished flinching.
social_impact: AWTS has changed the survival calculus of violence — augmented individuals with the system survive injuries that would kill anyone else, creating a durability gap between equipped and unequipped populations. The system has also enabled a reckless combat culture among those who have it, since the immediate consequences of being shot or stabbed are dramatically reduced. Long-term, the system's reservoir depletion is a significant concern — operators who sustain multiple injuries may exhaust their medical supplies without realizing it.
story_hooks: An AWTS-equipped operative sustained twelve gunshot wounds during an engagement and remained operational throughout — they only collapsed when the hemostatic reservoirs ran dry on wound thirteen.
Someone has developed a weapon specifically designed to overwhelm AWTS by creating dozens of superficial wounds simultaneously, depleting the system's reservoirs before delivering the killing blow.
